  note: >-
    The stored finite-range bound leaves one escape for a passive deposit: correlations set before or outside the
    descended metric, "initial data of the pre-metric sector". This result says what such data must carry. A
    deposit laid down with no geometric information is invariant under relabelling of its units, and then its
    second moments are two numbers; every dependence of a slice spectrum on the wavenumber is that of the map of
    the units into the slice, which is not part of the state. For cells that tile the slice, and for point cells
    on a periodic lattice, the spectrum is white, the stored finite-range class; for point cells that are not on
    a lattice the second number multiplies the placement's own structure factor, so the placement can carry a
    shape, and that case is in the statement as its boundary. The exact criterion for two numbers is transitivity
    of the invariance group on unordered pairs of units. So (argued) the escape needs a state whose invariance
    group separates pairs, that is, a deposit that already carries the separations of its units, or a placement
    of the units in the slice that carries the shape; a conformal structure alone leaves one exponent, the
    weight, which is the stored reading of the frozen phase. Kill condition written before the proof: an
    exchangeable state whose slice two-point function is not white plus a zero mode refutes the claim. For cells
    tiling the slice or on a lattice none exists (the constants and the vectors of zero sum are the only
    invariant subspaces that a covariance of this symmetry distinguishes); for point cells off a lattice two
    cells a quarter circle apart are such a state, so the claim is stated with that restriction. Transport-absent
    in its core (a symmetry argument valid for any algebra of observables); transport-convenient in clause (iv),
    where the fermion modes are null vectors of tower planes and the stored ladder states are the worked example.
    A white spectrum of the matter contrast is not a white spectrum of the curvature perturbation: the conversion
    depends on the descent slice, which the series leaves free, and it is not part of this result. The triple
    transitivity of the Lorentz group on null directions, mentioned in the technical text, is standard and is
    not used in the proof.
---
## formal
Let a deposit consist of $N \ge 2$ units labelled $1, \dots, N$ (cells of the descent slice, light rays, tower blocks), with Hermitian elements $O_{1}, \dots, O_{N}$ of its algebra of observables, and let a group $G$ of relabellings act on that algebra by automorphisms $\alpha_{g}$ with $\alpha_{g}(O_{i}) = O_{g i}$. For a state $\omega$ put
\[
C_{ij} = \tfrac12\,\omega(O_{i}O_{j} + O_{j}O_{i}) - \omega(O_{i})\,\omega(O_{j}), \qquad v = C_{11},
\]
and write $U$ for the $N \times N$ matrix with every entry $1$. The state is \emph{exchangeable} when $\omega \circ \alpha_{g} = \omega$ for every $g$ in the symmetric group of the labels.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Two numbers.)} If $\omega \circ \alpha_{g} = \omega$ for all $g \in G$ and $G$ is transitive on the labels and on unordered pairs of distinct labels (every doubly transitive group is, the symmetric group among them; for $N \ge 3$ the second condition implies the first), then $C = (v - c)\,1 + c\,U$ for one number $c$: $C$ has the eigenvalue $v - c$ on every vector of zero sum and $v + (N - 1)c$ on the constants, and positivity is $-v/(N - 1) \le c \le v$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(No shape.)} Let each unit sit in a slice with a real profile $g_{i}$, so that the slice field is $\phi(x) = \sum_{i}g_{i}(x)\bigl(O_{i} - \omega(O_{i})\bigr)$, and for a real test function $f$ let $f_{i} = \int f g_{i}$. Under the hypothesis of (i),
\[
\mathrm{Var}_{\omega}\bigl(\phi(f)\bigr) = (v - c)\sum_{i}f_{i}^{2} + c\Bigl(\sum_{i}f_{i}\Bigr)^{2}.
\]
The state enters through $v - c$ and $c$ alone; the dependence on $f$, and so on the wavenumber, is that of two quadratic forms fixed by the embedding. Two cases are white. (a) \emph{Cells that tile the slice}, $\sum_{i}g_{i} = 1$: then $\sum_{i}f_{i} = \int f = 0$ for every mode of nonzero wave vector, the variance is $(v - c)\sum_{i}f_{i}^{2}$, constant in $k$ below the inverse size of a cell and multiplied above it by the squared transform of the cells. (b) \emph{Point cells on a periodic lattice}, $g_{i} = V_{c}\,\delta(x - x_{i})$ at the points $x_{i}$ of a lattice of cell volume $V_{c}$: every cosine or sine mode of nonzero wave vector of the dual lattice has $\sum_{i}f_{i} = 0$, and $P(k) = (v - c)V_{c}$ for every such $k$. In both cases $\Delta^{2}(k) = k^{3}P/2\pi^{2} \propto k^{3}$ on those scales, the finite-range class of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.finite-range-descent-deposit-cannot-seed-cmb}, together with a term supported at $k = 0$. \emph{Boundary of the statement.} For point cells that are not on a lattice the second term does not vanish at nonzero wave vector: the sum of the cosine and sine variances is $V_{c}^{2}\bigl[(v - c)N + c\,N S_{\mathrm{pl}}(k)\bigr]$ with $S_{\mathrm{pl}}(k) = N^{-1}\bigl[(\sum_{i}\cos k\cdot x_{i})^{2} + (\sum_{i}\sin k\cdot x_{i})^{2}\bigr]$ the structure factor of the placement, and $c$ may be as large as $v$; so the spectrum then has the placement's shape, weighted by the state's second number. The smallest case: two cells at $x = 0$ and $x = L/4$ on a circle of length $L$; the modes $\cos(2\pi x/L)$ and $\cos(4\pi x/L)$ have $f = (1, 0)$ and $f = (1, -1)$ and variances $v$ and $2(v - c)$, whose ratio depends on $c$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The criterion.)} If $G$ is transitive on the labels but not on unordered pairs of distinct labels, let $A$ be the adjacency matrix of one orbit of $G$ on such pairs, of valency $d$. For $0 < |\varepsilon| < 1/d$ the matrix $1 + \varepsilon A$ is $G$-invariant, positive definite and not of the form in (i), and it is the covariance of a $G$-invariant state (the centred Gaussian measure with that covariance, the $O_{i}$ being the coordinates). So, for $G$ transitive on the labels, the two-number form holds for every $G$-invariant state exactly when $G$ is transitive on unordered pairs of distinct labels, and in general the number of free second moments is one more than the number of orbits of $G$ on such pairs.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Fermion modes.)} Let the units be $N$ fermion modes, $a_{i}^{*} = v_{i}$ and $a_{i} = w_{i}$ the null vectors of $N$ tower planes (Theorem \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}), with the symmetric group permuting the planes, and let $\omega$ be exchangeable. Then the one-particle matrix is $E_{ij} = \omega(a_{j}^{*}a_{i}) = (n - e)\delta_{ij} + e$ with $n$ and $e$ real, the pairing vanishes, $\omega(a_{i}a_{j}) = 0$ for all $i, j$, and in particular $-n/(N - 1) \le e \le (1 - n)/(N - 1)$, so $|e| \le 1/(N - 1)$ (the other eigenvalue of $E$ adds $n - 1 \le e \le n$). If $\omega$ is also quasi-free then, by the variance formula of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.quasi-free-deposit-is-vacuum-plus-shot-noise}(i), for every real symmetric one-body matrix $f$ and $N_{f} = \sum_{ij}f_{ij}a_{i}^{*}a_{j}$,
\[
\mathrm{Var}_{\omega}(N_{f}) = \alpha(1 - \alpha)\Tr f^{2} + e(1 - 2\alpha)\,\mathbf{1}^{T}f^{2}\mathbf{1} - e^{2}\bigl(\mathbf{1}^{T}f\mathbf{1}\bigr)^{2}, \qquad \alpha = n - e,
\]
$\mathbf{1}$ the vector with every entry $1$; for diagonal $f$ this is $(n(1 - n) + e^{2})\sum_{i}f_{i}^{2} - e^{2}(\sum_{i}f_{i})^{2}$, the form of (ii) with $v - c = n(1 - n) + e^{2}$ and $c = -e^{2}$, $|c| \le (N - 1)^{-2}$. The stored ladder states $\omega_{k}$ of $N$ blocks (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.ladder-states-are-locally-product-with-non-gaussian-fluctuations}(ii)), which are exchangeable and not quasi-free, have for the upper occupations $v = \tfrac kN(1 - \tfrac kN)$ and $c = \tfrac{k(k - 1)}{N(N - 1)} - \tfrac{k^{2}}{N^{2}}$, so $v + (N - 1)c = 0$ (the total is sharp) and $v - c = \tfrac{k(N - k)}{N(N - 1)}$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(A conformal structure leaves one exponent.)} The similarities $x \mapsto \lambda R(x) + b$ of a Euclidean slice ($\lambda > 0$, $R$ a product of reflections $x \mapsto -uxu^{-1}$ in $\Cl(3,0)$) are transitive on ordered pairs of distinct points. Hence a kernel $K(x, y)$ on distinct points that is invariant under them is constant, and a kernel of weight $\Delta$, $K(gx, gy) = \lambda_{g}^{-2\Delta}K(x, y)$, is a constant multiple of $Q(x - y)^{-\Delta}$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently a deposit that carries no geometric information, in the sense that its state is invariant under a group of relabellings of its units transitive on pairs, supplies two second moments: on a slice into which its units are placed as cells tiling the slice, or as point cells on a periodic lattice, it is white noise plus a term at $k = 0$, and in general the dependence on the wavenumber is that of the placement (the cells' form factor and, through $c$, the placement's structure factor), the same for every such state. \emph{Reading (argued).} A deposit set before the metric can therefore carry a spectrum other than the white one only if its invariance group separates pairs of units, that is, if the state already carries the separations of its units, or if the map of its units into the slice carries the shape; a conformal structure alone leaves one exponent, the weight. This result concerns the second moments of the deposit's matter observables; how a white energy spectrum converts into a spectrum of the curvature perturbation depends on the descent slice and is not decided here.

## technical
The stored finite-range bound closes passive deposits with correlations of finite range and leaves the pre-metric sector as the place where long-range correlations could be set. The question taken up here is what a pre-metric state must contain for that. If the deposit is laid down before any metric and with no geometric information, nothing distinguishes one pair of its units from another, and its state is invariant under relabelling. The covariance matrix of the units' observables then commutes with the permutation representation, which is the sum of the trivial representation and one irreducible representation, so it has two eigenvalues: one for the constant mode and one for everything else. Placing the units in a slice as cells that tile it, or as point cells on a lattice, gives white noise on every mode of nonzero wave vector, with the constant mode carrying the second number, and above the inverse cell size the squared transform of the cells. That is the whole of what the state contributes. The placement can contribute more: for point cells that are not on a lattice the second number multiplies the structure factor of the set of points, so a clustered or otherwise correlated placement shows its own shape in the spectrum; two cells a quarter of a circle apart already show it. The dependence on the wavenumber is in every case a property of the placement, the same for all such states. The criterion is exact: the two-number form holds for every invariant state precisely when the group is transitive on unordered pairs, and otherwise each further orbit on pairs is a further free second moment, as the nearest-neighbour covariance on a ring shows. For fermion modes exchangeability forces the pairing to vanish and bounds the coherence between two modes by $1/(N - 1)$; the quasi-free case is explicit, and the stored ladder states of the tower are the worked non-Gaussian example, with a sharp total and white fluctuations beneath it. Two groups of the series are of the transitive kind. The similarities of a slice, which the frozen point's stabiliser induces on its late-time boundary, are transitive on pairs of points, so an invariant kernel of weight zero is constant and a kernel of weight $\Delta$ is the single power $Q(x - y)^{-\Delta}$, index $2\Delta$: the stored reading in which the index is twice a weight and never negative on the unitary series (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.frozen-phase-spectrum-not-red}). The Lorentz group on the sphere of null directions is triply transitive (standard), so a state of light rays invariant under it is of the same kind. The Euclidean group of a slice is not transitive on pairs: its orbits are the separations, and an invariant covariance is a free function of the separation, which is the setting of the stored finite-range bound. So the pre-metric escape is not closed by this result, but it is narrowed (argued) to deposits that carry the separations of their units before the metric does, or whose units are laid into the slice by a map that itself carries the shape. Whiteness here is a statement about the matter observables; what it means for the curvature perturbation depends on the descent slice, which the series leaves free.

## lay
Suppose the event that began the universe scattered its energy into a great many cells before there was any notion of distance, so that no pair of cells was special. Then the pattern of fluctuations has only two numbers in it: how much one cell fluctuates, and how much any two cells fluctuate together. If the cells fill space, the result is featureless noise in the matter, the same at every scale, plus a uniform offset. The measured ripples of the early universe are not featureless: they have nearly equal strength on every scale, which is a very particular long-range pattern. So a deposit made before distance existed cannot hold that pattern unless it already knew which cells would be near which, or the way the cells were laid out in space supplied it; and featureless noise in the matter does not give the measured pattern under any of the ways of reading it off that have been examined (argued). Knowing only angles and shapes (a conformal structure) is not enough: it allows one exponent and nothing more.

## one-liner
A state invariant under a group of relabellings transitive on pairs of its units (exchangeable states among them) has covariance $(v - c)\,1 + c\,U$: on a slice tiled by its cells, or for point cells on a lattice, it is white noise plus a term at $k = 0$, all other dependence on the wavenumber being the placement's (for point cells off a lattice, the placement's structure factor through $c$); the criterion is exact, an exchangeable fermion state has no pairing and coherence at most $1/(N - 1)$, and similarity-invariant kernels are single powers, so a pre-metric deposit carries a spectrum only if it, or its placement, carries the separations of its units (argued).

proofs.proof-main.tex:
(i) Since $\omega \circ \alpha_{g} = \omega$ and $\alpha_{g}(O_{i}) = O_{gi}$, $C_{gi,gj} = C_{ij}$ for all $g \in G$. Transitivity on the labels gives $C_{ii} = v$ for all $i$. (For $N \ge 3$ transitivity on unordered pairs implies it: if the labels split into two nonempty invariant sets, the pairs inside one set and the pairs across the two are different orbits, and one set has two labels or the other does.) $C$ is symmetric, so $C_{ij}$ is a function of the unordered pair $\{i, j\}$, constant on the single orbit: $C_{ij} = c$ for $i \ne j$. Then $C = (v - c)1 + cU$; $U$ has eigenvalue $N$ on the constants and $0$ on the vectors of zero sum, which gives the two eigenvalues, and $C \ge 0$ (a covariance) is $v - c \ge 0$ and $v + (N - 1)c \ge 0$. The check computes the orbits by closure for the symmetric group on four labels, the affine groups of the fields of five and seven elements (doubly transitive), the group $x \mapsto a^{2}x + b$ of seven elements (transitive on unordered pairs with two orbits on ordered pairs), and the cyclic and dihedral groups of six (three orbits each), and verifies the eigenvalues and the positivity ends.

(ii) $\phi(f) = \sum_{i}f_{i}(O_{i} - \omega(O_{i}))$, so $\mathrm{Var}_{\omega}(\phi(f)) = \sum_{ij}f_{i}C_{ij}f_{j} = (v - c)\sum_{i}f_{i}^{2} + c(\sum_{i}f_{i})^{2}$ by (i). If the profiles tile the slice, $\sum_{i}g_{i} = 1$, then $\sum_{i}f_{i} = \int f\sum_{i}g_{i} = \int f$, which vanishes for a cosine or sine mode of nonzero wave vector; the remaining term $(v - c)\sum_{i}f_{i}^{2}$ depends on $k$ only through the transforms of the cells, which tend to their volumes for $k$ below the inverse cell size. On a periodic lattice a cosine or sine mode of nonzero dual wave vector sums to zero over the cells, and $\sum_{i}f_{i}^{2}$ is the number of cells times the mean square of the mode, so the variance per unit volume and unit mean square is $(v - c)V_{c}$, independent of the wave vector. A spectrum independent of $k$ has $\Delta^{2} \propto k^{3}$, the limiting form of the stored bound of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.finite-range-descent-deposit-cannot-seed-cmb}(i) for a covariance supported within one cell. For point cells at arbitrary points, $f_{i} = V_{c}\cos(k\cdot x_{i})$ or $V_{c}\sin(k\cdot x_{i})$, and adding the two variances gives $V_{c}^{2}[(v - c)N + c\,((\sum_{i}\cos k\cdot x_{i})^{2} + (\sum_{i}\sin k\cdot x_{i})^{2})]$, which is the boundary statement; the second bracket vanishes at nonzero $k$ exactly on the scales where the points have no structure factor, as on a lattice away from its dual. For two cells at $0$ and $L/4$ the cosines are $(1, 0)$ and $(1, -1)$, and $f^{T}Cf$ is $v$ and $2(v - c)$. The check verifies the equal variances on the three cosine modes of a ring of six cells (the cosines are fixed by their recurrence, with rational values) and on the seven Walsh modes of eight cells, for several $(v, c)$. A further check function takes a ring of six sites: point cells on the whole ring and on a sublattice (no $c$ term except on the dual lattice), cells that tile the ring with equal and with unequal sizes (no $c$ term at nonzero $k$, and $(v - c)$ times the cells' form factor), point cells at the sites $0, 1, 3$ (the $c$ term is $c$ times $N S_{\mathrm{pl}} = 1, 3, 1$ on the three modes, so the first two modes agree only for $c = 0$), and the two cells a quarter circle apart.

(iii) $A$ commutes with the permutation matrices of $G$ because $G$ permutes the orbit. Each row of $A$ has $d$ entries $1$, so $1 + \varepsilon A$ is strictly diagonally dominant for $|\varepsilon| < 1/d$ and hence positive definite. It is not $(v - c)1 + cU$: its off-diagonal entries take the two values $\varepsilon$ and $0$, both occurring since there is a second orbit. A centred Gaussian measure on $\mathbb{R}^{N}$ with covariance $1 + \varepsilon A$ is invariant under the coordinate permutations of $G$, and its coordinates are observables $O_{i}$ permuted by $G$. Conversely (i). The symmetric $G$-invariant matrices are spanned by $1$ and the adjacency matrices of the orbits on unordered pairs, which gives the count. The check exhibits the ring of six cells with nearest-neighbour $A$, $\varepsilon = \tfrac14$: variances per unit norm $\tfrac54, \tfrac34, \tfrac12$ on the three cosine modes.

(iv) The transposition of planes $i$ and $j$ is an automorphism exchanging $a_{i}$ and $a_{j}$; invariance gives $E_{ij} = E_{ji}$, and $E$ is Hermitian for the conjugation of its scalars, so $E_{ij}$ is real; double transitivity gives $E_{ii} = n$ and $E_{ij} = e$ for $i \ne j$. For the pairing, $\omega(a_{i}a_{j}) = \omega(a_{j}a_{i})$ by the same transposition and $a_{i}a_{j} = -a_{j}a_{i}$ (the vectors $w_{i}$ anticommute, Theorem \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}), so it vanishes for $i \ne j$; and $a_{i}^{2} = Q(w_{i}) = 0$. From $0 \le E \le 1$ and the eigenvalues $n - e$ and $n + (N - 1)e$ of $E$: $0 \le n + (N - 1)e \le 1$, which is the stated bound, and $0 \le n - e \le 1$, which is the other. For quasi-free $\omega$ the pairing vanishes, so the state is gauge-invariant and $\mathrm{Var}(N_{f}) = \Tr(fEf(1 - E))$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.quasi-free-deposit-is-vacuum-plus-shot-noise}(i)); with $E = \alpha 1 + eU$ and $\Tr(f^{2}U) = \Tr(fUf) = \mathbf{1}^{T}f^{2}\mathbf{1}$, $\Tr(fUfU) = (\mathbf{1}^{T}f\mathbf{1})^{2}$ the trace is the displayed expression; for diagonal $f$, $\alpha(1 - \alpha) + e(1 - 2\alpha) = n(1 - n) + e^{2}$. The check realises four modes in $\Cl(4,4)$ and the state of one quantum in the symmetric mode, $\psi = (\sum_{j}v_{j})\prod_{j}(1 - n_{j})$, a pure quasi-free state: the transposition and the four-cycle of planes fix $\psi$; $E_{ij} = \tfrac14$ for all $i, j$, the upper end $e = (1 - n)/(N - 1)$; the pairing vanishes; the number covariances are $v = \tfrac{3}{16}$, $c = -\tfrac{1}{16}$; and the displayed variance agrees with the direct one for diagonal and for non-diagonal $f$. For the ladder states, permutation symmetry and the moments $\omega_{k}(n_{u_{i}}) = k/N$, $\omega_{k}(n_{u_{i}}n_{u_{j}}) = k(k - 1)/(N(N - 1))$ are stored (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.ladder-states-are-locally-product-with-non-gaussian-fluctuations}(ii)); since $n_{u_{i}}^{2} = n_{u_{i}}$, $v = \tfrac kN(1 - \tfrac kN)$, and the two combinations follow by arithmetic. The check recomputes them on two and three blocks.

(v) Given distinct $x, y$ and distinct $x', y'$ put $d = y - x$, $d' = y' - x'$, $\lambda = (Q(d')/Q(d))^{1/2}$ and $u = \lambda d - d'$. If $u = 0$ the map $p \mapsto \lambda(p - x) + x'$ carries $(x, y)$ to $(x', y')$. Otherwise $Q(\lambda d) = Q(d')$ gives $u \cdot (\lambda d + d') = 0$, so the reflection $z \mapsto -uzu^{-1}$ exchanges $\lambda d$ and $d'$, and $p \mapsto -u\,\lambda(p - x)\,u^{-1} + x'$ does it. So the similarities are transitive on ordered pairs of distinct points. An invariant kernel then takes one value. For weight $\Delta$, $K(x, y)\,Q(x - y)^{\Delta}$ is invariant, since $Q(gx - gy) = \lambda_{g}^{2}Q(x - y)$, hence constant. The check carries three rational pairs to three prescribed pairs with $\lambda = \tfrac73, \tfrac37, \tfrac{11}{9}$ and verifies the scaling of $Q(x - y)^{-\Delta}$ for $\Delta = 0, 1, -1, 2$. The index of a slice correlator homogeneous of degree $-2\Delta$ is $2\Delta$, and on the frozen phase the leading weight gives a non-negative index (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.frozen-phase-spectrum-not-red}); that proposition is cited for the reading and is not used in the proof of (v).

The consequence is (i) to (iii) read for a deposit whose units are placed in a slice: the state supplies $v - c$ and $c$, and every dependence on the wavenumber is in the quadratic forms $\sum_{i}f_{i}^{2}$ and $(\sum_{i}f_{i})^{2}$ of the placement, the second of which vanishes at nonzero $k$ for tilings and lattices and is the placement's structure factor otherwise. The reading that follows it is argued: it lists the two places a shape can come from, the state's invariance group and the placement, and does not exclude either.

    of its two labels has that entry zero.
(4) Similarities.  In Cl(3,0) a reflection is x -> -u x u^(-1); translation, reflection and dilatation carry the
    pair (x, y) to a prescribed pair (x', y') (double transitivity, on a rational sample with |y' - x'|/|y - x| =
    7/3), so an invariant kernel takes one value off the diagonal; the kernels Q(x - y)^(-D) (D = 0, 1, -1, 2)
    scale by lambda^(-2D) under the same map: one exponent, no shape beyond it.
(5) Placements (the boundary of clause (ii)).  Ring of six sites, modes m = 1, 2, 3.  Point cells on the whole
    ring or on the sublattice {0, 2, 4}: the c term vanishes off the dual lattice.  Cells tiling the ring, equal
    ({0,1},{2,3},{4,5}) or unequal ({0},{1,2,3},{4,5}): sum f_i = 0 at nonzero m and the variance is (v - c) times
    the cells' form factor (9, 3, 0 and 8, 2, 2).  Point cells at the sites 0, 1, 3, not a lattice: the c term is
    c times N S_pl = 1, 3, 1, so modes 1 and 2 agree only for c = 0.  Two cells a quarter circle apart: variances
    v and 2(v - c).
Every block of assertions is labelled, so a failure names its clause.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
import itertools

import GA
from tp_premise import premise


def _mark(label, ok):
    """Record one labelled assertion, so that a failure names its clause."""
    GA.check(label, bool(ok))
    return bool(ok)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- permutation groups and orbitals
def _closure(gens, n):
    ident = tuple(range(n))
    seen = {ident}
    frontier = [ident]
    while frontier:
        nxt = []
        for g in frontier:
            for h in gens:
                gh = tuple(h[g[i]] for i in range(n))
                if gh not in seen:
                    seen.add(gh)
                    nxt.append(gh)
        frontier = nxt
    return seen


def _orbitals(group, n, symmetrise=True):
    """Orbits on pairs (i, j), i != j; with symmetrise, (i, j) and (j, i) are joined."""
    left = {(i, j) for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if i != j}
    orbs = []
    while left:
        p = next(iter(left))
        orb = set()
        for g in group:
            q = (g[p[0]], g[p[1]])
            orb.add(q)
            if symmetrise:
                orb.add((q[1], q[0]))
        orbs.append(orb)
        left -= orb
    return orbs


def _affine(p, mults):
    return [tuple((a * x + b) % p for x in range(p)) for a in mults for b in range(p)]


def _mat(v, c, n):
    return [[(v if i == j else c) for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]


def _quad(C, f, g=None):
    g = f if g is None else g
    return sum((f[i] * C[i][j] * g[j] for i in range(len(f)) for j in range(len(g))), F(0))


def _apply(C, f):
    return [sum((C[i][j] * f[j] for j in range(len(f))), F(0)) for i in range(len(f))]


def check_doubly_transitive_relabelling_leaves_two_numbers():
    marks = []
    sym4 = _closure([(1, 0, 2, 3), (1, 2, 3, 0)], 4)
    aff5 = _closure(_affine(5, [1, 2, 3, 4]), 5)
    aff7 = _closure(_affine(7, [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]), 7)
    cyc6 = _closure([(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0)], 6)

    sq7 = _closure(_affine(7, [1, 2, 4]), 7)
    ok = (len(sym4), len(aff5), len(aff7), len(cyc6), len(dih6), len(sq7)) == (24, 20, 42, 6, 12, 21)
    counts = [len(_orbitals(g, n)) for g, n in ((sym4, 4), (aff5, 5), (aff7, 7), (cyc6, 6), (dih6, 6), (sq7, 7))]
    ok = ok and counts == [1, 1, 1, 3, 3, 1]
    ok = ok and len(_orbitals(sq7, 7, symmetrise=False)) == 2 and len(_orbitals(aff7, 7, symmetrise=False)) == 1
    marks.append(_mark("(i), (iii) group orders and the orbits on unordered and on ordered pairs", ok))
    ok = True
    # every invariant symmetric matrix of a doubly transitive group is (v - c) 1 + c U: check invariance and spectrum
    for n, group in ((4, sym4), (5, aff5), (7, aff7)):
        for v, c in ((F(3), F(1)), (F(2), F(-1, 3)), (F(5, 7), F(2, 9))):
            C = _mat(v, c, n)
            ok = ok and all(C[g[i]][g[j]] == C[i][j] for g in group for i in range(n) for j in range(n))
            ones = [F(1)] * n
            ok = ok and _apply(C, ones) == [v + (n - 1) * c] * n
            for f in ([F(1), F(-1)] + [F(0)] * (n - 2), [F(2), F(-3), F(1)] + [F(0)] * (n - 3),
                      [F(k) - F(n - 1, 2) for k in range(n)]):
                ok = ok and sum(f) == 0 and _apply(C, f) == [(v - c) * x for x in f]
            for f in ([F(k * k + 1, 3) for k in range(n)], [F((-2) ** k, 5) for k in range(n)]):
                ok = ok and _quad(C, f) == (v - c) * sum(x * x for x in f) + c * sum(f) ** 2
    marks.append(_mark("(i) invariance of (v - c) 1 + c U, its two eigenvalues, and the variance of arbitrary profiles", ok))
    ok = True
    # positivity ends: c = v kills the sum-zero modes, c = -v/(N - 1) kills the constant
    for n in (4, 5, 7):
        v = F(3)
        ok = ok and _apply(_mat(v, v, n), [F(1), F(-1)] + [F(0)] * (n - 2)) == [F(0)] * n
        ok = ok and _apply(_mat(v, -v / (n - 1), n), [F(1)] * n) == [F(0)] * n
        ok = ok and _quad(_mat(v, -v / (n - 1) - F(1, 100), n), [F(1)] * n) < 0
    marks.append(_mark("(i) positivity ends c = v and c = -v/(N - 1)", ok))
    assert all(marks)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- CAR side, in Cl(N, N)
def _dag(x, sq):
    out = {}
    for b, c in x.items():
        g = len(b)
        s = (-1) ** (g * (g - 1) // 2) * (-1) ** sum(1 for i in b if sq[i] == -1)
        out[b] = c * s
    return {b: c for b, c in out.items() if c != 0}


def _prod(xs, sq):
    r = GA.sc(1)
    for x in xs:
        r = GA.mul(r, x, sq)
    return r


def _ip(x, y):
    return sum((c * y.get(b, 0) for b, c in x.items()), F(0))


def _modes(nm):
    sq = tuple([1, -1] * nm)
    v = [GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.add(GA.gen(2 * j), GA.gen(2 * j + 1))) for j in range(nm)]
    w = [GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.sub(GA.gen(2 * j), GA.gen(2 * j + 1))) for j in range(nm)]
    n = [GA.mul(v[j], w[j], sq) for j in range(nm)]
    return sq, v, w, n


def _relabel(x, perm, sq):
    """The algebra automorphism that sends plane j to plane perm[j]."""
    out = {}
    for b, c in x.items():
        img = _prod([GA.gen(2 * perm[i // 2] + i % 2) for i in b], sq)
        out = GA.add(out, GA.scal(c, img))
    return out


def check_exchangeable_fermion_states():
    marks = []
    premise("tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors")
    premise("synthesis.quasi-free-deposit-is-vacuum-plus-shot-noise")
    premise("synthesis.ladder-states-are-locally-product-with-non-gaussian-fluctuations")
    ok = True
    nm = 4
    sq, v, w, n = _modes(nm)
    for i in range(nm):
        for j in range(nm):
            anti = GA.add(GA.mul(v[i], w[j], sq), GA.mul(w[j], v[i], sq))
            ok = ok and anti == (GA.sc(1) if i == j else {})
            ok = ok and GA.anticommutes(v[i], v[j], sq) and GA.anticommutes(w[i], w[j], sq)
    marks.append(_mark("(iv) anticommutation relations of the null vectors of four tower planes", ok))
    ok = True
    vac = _prod([GA.sub(GA.sc(1), n[j]) for j in range(nm)], sq)
    psi = GA.mul(GA.add(*v), vac, sq)
    nrm = _ip(psi, psi)
    ok = ok and nrm != 0
    # exchangeable: the transposition of planes 0 and 1, and the 4-cycle, fix psi
    ok = ok and _relabel(psi, (1, 0, 2, 3), sq) == psi and _relabel(psi, (1, 2, 3, 0), sq) == psi

    def ev(X):
        return _ip(psi, GA.mul(X, psi, sq)) / nrm

    E = [[ev(GA.mul(v[j], w[i], sq)) for j in range(nm)] for i in range(nm)]
    ok = ok and all(E[i][j] == F(1, 4) for i in range(nm) for j in range(nm))
    nn, e = F(1, 4), F(1, 4)
    ok = ok and e == (1 - nn) / (nm - 1) and -nn / (nm - 1) <= e
    ok = ok and nn - 1 <= e <= nn                      # the other eigenvalue, n - e, lies in [0, 1] as well
    ok = ok and all(ev(GA.mul(w[i], w[j], sq)) == 0 and ev(GA.mul(v[i], v[j], sq)) == 0
                    for i in range(nm) for j in range(nm))
    var = ev(GA.mul(n[0], n[0], sq)) - ev(n[0]) ** 2
    cov = ev(GA.mul(n[0], n[1], sq)) - ev(n[0]) * ev(n[1])
    ok = ok and (var, cov) == (F(3, 16), F(-1, 16)) and var + (nm - 1) * cov == 0 and var - cov == F(1, 4)
    ok = ok and all(ev(GA.mul(n[i], n[j], sq)) - ev(n[i]) * ev(n[j]) == cov
                    for i in range(nm) for j in range(nm) if i != j)
    marks.append(_mark("(iv) symmetric one-quantum state: fixed by relabellings, E_ij = 1/4, no pairing, number covariances", ok))
    ok = True
    # the stored quasi-free variance Tr(f E f (1 - E)) for diagonal f: (n(1-n) + e^2) sum f^2 - e^2 (sum f)^2
    for f in ([F(1), F(-1), F(0), F(0)], [F(2), F(1, 3), F(-5), F(7, 2)], [F(1)] * 4):
        tr = sum((f[i] * E[i][j] * f[j] * ((F(1) if i == j else F(0)) - E[j][i])
                  for i in range(nm) for j in range(nm)), F(0))
        direct = ev(_prod([GA.add(*[GA.scal(f[i], n[i]) for i in range(nm)])] * 2, sq)) \
            - ev(GA.add(*[GA.scal(f[i], n[i]) for i in range(nm)])) ** 2
        formula = (nn * (1 - nn) + e * e) * sum(x * x for x in f) - e * e * sum(f) ** 2
        ok = ok and tr == direct == formula
    # general one-body f (real symmetric): Var = a(1-a) Tr f^2 + e(1-2a) <1, f^2 1> - e^2 <1, f 1>^2, a = n - e
    for fm in ([[F(1), F(2), F(0), F(-1)], [F(2), F(0), F(1, 2), F(3)], [F(0), F(1, 2), F(-2), F(1)],
                [F(-1), F(3), F(1), F(5)]],
               [[F(0), F(1), F(1), F(1)], [F(1), F(0), F(1), F(1)], [F(1), F(1), F(0), F(1)],
                [F(1), F(1), F(1), F(0)]]):
        Nf = GA.add(*[GA.scal(fm[i][j], GA.mul(v[i], w[j], sq)) for i in range(nm) for j in range(nm)])
        direct = ev(GA.mul(Nf, Nf, sq)) - ev(Nf) ** 2
        f2 = [[sum(fm[i][k] * fm[k][j] for k in range(nm)) for j in range(nm)] for i in range(nm)]
        a = nn - e
        formula = a * (1 - a) * sum(f2[i][i] for i in range(nm)) \
            + e * (1 - 2 * a) * sum(f2[i][j] for i in range(nm) for j in range(nm)) \
            - e * e * sum(fm[i][j] for i in range(nm) for j in range(nm)) ** 2
        ok = ok and direct == formula
    marks.append(_mark("(iv) quasi-free variance for diagonal and for general one-body f", ok))
    ok = True
    # an antisymmetric matrix invariant under the transposition of its two labels vanishes there
    for p in (F(3, 7), F(-2), F(0)):
        P01, P10 = p, -p            # antisymmetry
        invariant = (P10 == P01)    # invariance under (0 1)
        ok = ok and (invariant == (p == 0))
    marks.append(_mark("(iv) an antisymmetric entry invariant under the transposition of its labels vanishes", ok))
    ok = True
    # the stored ladder states: permutation symmetric, covariance of the upper occupations
    for Nb in (2, 3):

        psik = P
        for k in range(1, Nb + 1):
            psik = GA.mul(Ks, psik, sqb)

            def evk(X):
                return _ip(psik, GA.mul(X, psik, sqb)) / nk

            vv = evk(GA.mul(nb[1], nb[1], sqb)) - evk(nb[1]) ** 2
            cc = evk(GA.mul(nb[1], nb[3], sqb)) - evk(nb[1]) * evk(nb[3])
            ok = ok and vv == F(k, Nb) * (1 - F(k, Nb))
            ok = ok and cc == F(k * (k - 1), Nb * (Nb - 1)) - F(k, Nb) ** 2
            ok = ok and vv + (Nb - 1) * cc == 0 and vv - cc == F(k * (Nb - k), Nb * (Nb - 1))
    marks.append(_mark("(iv) the stored ladder states: v, c, sharp total, v - c", ok))
    assert all(marks)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- similarities of a Euclidean slice, in Cl(3,0)
def _vec(a):
    return GA.add(*[GA.scal(F(a[i]), GA.gen(i)) for i in range(3)]) if any(a) else {}


def _coords(x):
    return [x.get((i,), F(0)) for i in range(3)]


def _q(x, sq):
    return GA.mul(x, x, sq).get((), F(0))


def _reflect(u, x, sq):
    """x -> -u x u^(-1), the reflection in the plane orthogonal to u."""
    return GA.scal(F(-1) / _q(u, sq), GA.mul(GA.mul(u, x, sq), u, sq))


def check_similarities_are_doubly_transitive_and_leave_one_exponent():
    marks = []
    premise("synthesis.frozen-phase-spectrum-not-red")
    sq = GA.sig(3, 0)
    ok = True
    samples = [((1, 0, 2), (2, 2, 4), (5, -1, 0), (7, 2, 6)),      # d = (1,2,2), d' = (2,3,6): 3 -> 7
               ((0, 0, 0), (2, 3, 6), (1, 1, 1), (2, 3, 3)),       # 7 -> 3
               ((4, 4, 7), (5, 8, 15), (0, 0, 0), (6, 6, 7))]      # d = (1,4,8) norm 9, d' = (6,6,7) norm 11
    for xs, ys, xt, yt in samples:
        x, y, x2, y2 = _vec(xs), _vec(ys), _vec(xt), _vec(yt)
        d, d2 = GA.sub(y, x), GA.sub(y2, x2)
        lam2 = _q(d2, sq) / _q(d, sq)
        lam = None
        for num in range(1, 40):
            for den in range(1, 40):
                if F(num, den) ** 2 == lam2:
                    lam = F(num, den)
        ok = ok and lam is not None
        u = GA.sub(GA.scal(lam, d), d2)

        def g(p):
            z = GA.scal(lam, GA.sub(p, x))
            z = _reflect(u, z, sq) if u else z
            return GA.add(z, x2)

        ok = ok and g(x) == x2 and g(y) == y2
        # the map is a similarity of ratio lam: squared distances scale by lam^2 on further rational points
        pts = [_vec(p) for p in ((3, -2, 5), (0, 7, 1), (-4, 4, 9), (1, 1, 1))]
        for a in pts:
            for b in pts:
                ok = ok and _q(GA.sub(g(a), g(b)), sq) == lam2 * _q(GA.sub(a, b), sq)
                if a != b:
                    r2 = _q(GA.sub(a, b), sq)
                    for D in (0, 1, -1, 2):
                        ok = ok and _q(GA.sub(g(a), g(b)), sq) ** (-D) == lam2 ** (-D) * r2 ** (-D)
        # a reflection preserves the square
        ok = ok and all(_q(_reflect(_vec((1, 2, 2)), a, sq), sq) == _q(a, sq) for a in pts)
    marks.append(_mark("(v) similarities carry a pair to a prescribed pair and scale Q(x - y)^(-D) by lambda^(-2D)", ok))
    assert all(marks)


def check_placements_tiling_lattice_and_off_lattice():
    """The boundary of clause (ii).  Ring of six sites, modes m = 1, 2, 3; cos(pi j/3) is rational and
    sin(pi j/3) = (sqrt 3/2) s_j with s_j in {0, 1, 1, 0, -1, -1}, so squares of sine sums are (3/4)(sum s)^2."""
    marks = []
    n = 6
    cos1 = [F(1), F(1, 2), F(-1, 2), F(-1), F(-1, 2), F(1, 2)]
    sin1 = [0, 1, 1, 0, -1, -1]

    def cs(m, j):
        return cos1[(m * j) % n], sin1[(m * j) % n]

    def power(cells, v, c, m):
        """Var(cosine moment) + Var(sine moment) for cells given as lists of sites (profile 1 on its sites)."""
        fc = [sum((cs(m, j)[0] for j in cell), F(0)) for cell in cells]
        fs = [sum(cs(m, j)[1] for j in cell) for cell in cells]
        sq = sum(x * x for x in fc) + F(3, 4) * sum(x * x for x in fs)
        tot = sum(fc) ** 2 + F(3, 4) * sum(fs) ** 2
        return (v - c) * sq + c * tot, sq, tot

    ok = True
    # point cells on the whole ring and on the sublattice {0, 2, 4}: no c term off the dual lattice
    for v, c in ((F(3), F(1)), (F(2), F(-2, 5)), (F(5), F(5))):
        full = [[j] for j in range(n)]
        ok = ok and [power(full, v, c, m) for m in (1, 2, 3)] == [((v - c) * 6, F(6), F(0))] * 3
        sub = [[0], [2], [4]]
        ok = ok and [power(sub, v, c, m)[2] for m in (1, 2, 3)] == [F(0), F(0), F(9)]
        ok = ok and power(sub, v, c, 1)[0] == power(sub, v, c, 2)[0] == (v - c) * 3
    marks.append(_mark("(ii) point cells on a periodic lattice: white, the c term only on the dual lattice", ok))
    ok = True
    # cells that tile the ring, equal or unequal: sum f_i = 0 on every nonzero mode; only the cells' form factor
    for cells, forms in (([[0, 1], [2, 3], [4, 5]], [F(9), F(3), F(0)]),
                         ([[0], [1, 2, 3], [4, 5]], [F(8), F(2), F(2)])):
        for v, c in ((F(3), F(1)), (F(2), F(-2, 5))):
            got = [power(cells, v, c, m) for m in (1, 2, 3)]
            ok = ok and [g[2] for g in got] == [F(0)] * 3
            ok = ok and [g[1] for g in got] == forms and [g[0] for g in got] == [(v - c) * x for x in forms]
    marks.append(_mark("(ii) cells tiling the slice: no c term at nonzero k, (v - c) times the cells' form factor", ok))
    ok = True
    # point cells off a lattice, sites {0, 1, 3}: the c term is c times the placement's structure factor
    off = [[0], [1], [3]]
    for v, c in ((F(3), F(1)), (F(2), F(-2, 5)), (F(1), F(0))):
        got = [power(off, v, c, m) for m in (1, 2, 3)]
        ok = ok and [g[1] for g in got] == [F(3)] * 3 and [g[2] for g in got] == [F(1), F(3), F(1)]
        ok = ok and [g[0] for g in got] == [3 * (v - c) + c, 3 * (v - c) + 3 * c, 3 * (v - c) + c]
        ok = ok and ((got[0][0] == got[1][0]) == (c == 0))
    marks.append(_mark("(ii) boundary: point cells off a lattice carry the placement's structure factor through c", ok))
    ok = True
    # smallest case: two cells at x = 0 and x = L/4 on a circle; modes cos(2 pi x/L), cos(4 pi x/L)
    for v, c in ((F(3), F(1)), (F(2), F(-1)), (F(4), F(4))):
        C = _mat(v, c, 2)
        ok = ok and _quad(C, [F(1), F(0)]) == v and _quad(C, [F(1), F(-1)]) == 2 * (v - c)
        ok = ok and ((_quad(C, [F(1), F(-1)]) == 2 * _quad(C, [F(1), F(0)])) == (c == 0))
    marks.append(_mark("(ii) boundary: two cells a quarter circle apart, variances v and 2(v - c)", ok))
    assert all(marks)
